neighbours.label: '-colored' or 'oured' in the idiom 'rose-colored glasses', not other '-colored' compounds
fire: Many voters remember the old days through rose-colored glasses.
Don't view your first job through rose-tinted or rose-colored lenses.
She always saw her hometown through rose-coloured glasses.
Critics say the report looks at the economy through rose-colored glasses.
His memoir paints the war years with a rose-colored brush.
Fans tend to watch those old teams through rose-colored glasses.
Nobody here wears rose-colored glasses about the budget.
We shouldn't look at that decade through rose-coloured spectacles.
quiet: Many voters remember the old days through faded photographs.
Don't view your first job through narrow or blue-colored lenses.
She always saw her hometown through a dusty window.
Critics say the report looks at the economy through a green-colored chart.
His memoir paints the war years with a dark brush.
Fans tend to watch those old teams through grainy video.
Nobody here wears sunglasses at the budget meeting.
We shouldn't look at that decade through cream-colored curtains.

notes: Card: ' of' x6, '-colored' x3, '4' x3, ' up' x2, 'oured', 71% in the echo regime. Probes: rose-colored 0.776, rose-coloured 0.725; 'Red-colored paint' 0.010, 'through dark glasses' 0.015. Bible references ('4' in Revelation 4:11 scored 1.027) and ' of' are outside this label, so it covers one of at least two clusters.
